To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HDL and its apo, APO, inhibit aortic smooth muscle proliferation by activating Cox-2 and stimulating the synthesis of the prostacylin IP receptor ligand prostacyclin.
the antimitotic effects of HDL are mediated by the prostacyclin (IP) receptor.

HDL, APOE and their N-terminal domains inhibit S-phase entry in murine and human aortic smooth cells by stimulating Cox- 2 expression, leading prostacyclin synthesis, and IP-dependent inhibition of cyclin A gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which APOE and the HDL receptor, SR-BI, mediate their effects on cell growth.
the mechanisms by which HDL and AOPs modulate the cell cycle in vascular smooth muscle cells and the potential relevance to atherosclerosis.
the role of HDL and apoA-I in vascular biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HDL, through APOE, activates the IP receptor, which in turn activates the Cox-2 promoter.
APOE, HDL, and the IP receptor are all linked to the Cox-2 pathway.
the antiproliferative and antimitogenic effects of APOE and HDL on vascular smooth muscle cells is mediated through a Cox-2-dependent pathway, leading to activation of the IP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HDL, APOE and their N-terminal domains, as well as HDL-associated PAF, inhibit aortic smooth muscle S-phase entry by suppressing Cox-2 expression and inhibiting the cyclin A-dependent pathway, and that this inhibition is dependent upon the activation of the IP receptor.
the antiproliferative effect of HDL is due, at least in part, to the activation of the prostaglandin I2 receptor, IP, by HDL-associated APOE.
the antiproliferative effects of HDL are mediated by the N-terminal domain of apo APOE, which is responsible for HDL binding to its receptor, the LDL receptor-related protein 1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-proliferative effects of APOE and HDL are mediated by the Cox-2-dependent production of prostacyclin, which activates the IP receptor.
HDL and its apolipoprotein E are antimitogenic in aortic smooth muscle and that this effect is mediated by the IP receptor.
APOE is a key regulator of cell cycle progression in atherosclerotic lesions.
